annotations.text:
Orbit v2 — pick one direction.

Same screen four ways: same data, same logic, four different answers to colour and containers. Pick one and I build the whole system from it (tokens, shadcn primitives, every route).

A · DAYLIGHT — light neutral canvas, one violet accent, a colour per domain. Cards are white with a hairline and a 1px shadow; this is the shadcn shape done properly.

Why: reads as a real product, ages well, easiest to keep consistent across five routes.
Tradeoff: the safest of the four — it will not stop anyone scrolling.

B · NOCTURNE — near-black ink with electric violet, cyan, pink and mint. Colour carries the data; a soft light-source glow sits behind the hero only.

Why: keeps the dark app you already have but makes it lively instead of grey, and the rings finally look like the point.
Tradeoff: gradients need discipline or it drifts into the same AI-dashboard look you are trying to leave.

C · BLOCKS — no cards at all. Full-bleed colour fields, 2px rules, huge Archivo numerals on paper white.

Why: the most memorable and the most ownable; nobody else's dashboard looks like this.
Tradeoff: loud, and dense screens (finance tables, statement imports) will fight it.

D · BLOOM — light and soft: tinted panels instead of bordered cards, one tint per domain, pill controls, deep plum accent.

Why: the friendliest and the most 'daily habit' of the four; colour tells you which system you are in without a label.
Tradeoff: tints eat contrast if the palette slips, and it is the least 'instrument' of the set.
